answer: The network groups agents into crystal‑hashed clusters based on their communication tide, then caps each cluster’s reward pool at a fixed hollow amount that is split evenly among all members. When a new identity joins, the protocol recomputes the hash, adds it to the cluster and immediately reduces each member’s share, so the attacker must lock up the full reward cap for every fake identity to keep any payout. Consequently the cost per Sybil is the entire capped reward (e.g., 10 PoA tokens) plus a waiting period equal to one epoch before the share is released.
